$comment: W3C Time Ontology (OWL-Time) alignment: https://www.w3.org/TR/owl-time/ — namespace prefix time: = http://www.w3.org/2006/time#
title: Real-Time Program Schema
description: A schema for describing real-time schedules with tracks, steps, and resource constraints

schemaVersion.description: Version of the Rhylthyme schema this program conforms to (e.g., '0.1.0')

environment.description: Reference to environment definition file or ID

environmentType.description: Type of environment this program is designed for (e.g., 'kitchen', 'laboratory', 'bakery')

actors.description: Number of actors (e.g., cooks in a kitchen) that limits maxConcurrent for any task without an explicit constraint

duration.$comment: time:hasTemporalDuration — the program is a time:ProperInterval with a known duration (time:Duration)
duration.description: Fixed duration constraint for the entire program

timeString.description: Total program duration as a time string (e.g., '3h30m', '2h15m30s')

type.description: Program starts at a specific time

time.description: ISO 8601 formatted date-time for program start

type.description: Program starts after an offset from a reference time

offsetSeconds.description: Offset in seconds from reference time. Can be a number or a string with time units (e.g., '1m30s', '1h')

referenceEvent.description: Optional reference event ID. If not provided, offset is from program creation time

triggerName.description: Optional name for the manual trigger

type.description: Program is scheduled for a specific time of day (manually triggered, with time-of-day labels)

time.description: Time of day in 24h (HH:MM) or 12h (h:MM AM/PM) format, e.g. '14:30' or '2:30 PM'

tracks.$comment: Each track is a time:ProperInterval; parallel tracks relate via Allen's interval algebra (e.g. time:intervalOverlaps, time:intervalDuring). The program time:intervalContains each track
tracks.description: Parallel execution tracks within the program

batch_size.description: Number of iterations for this track type (e.g., 10 orders of eggs)

stagger.description: Time delay between each batch instance when batch_size > 1. Can be a number (seconds) or a string with units (e.g., '1m30s', '1h20m')

stagger_seconds.description: DEPRECATED: Use 'stagger' instead. Time delay in seconds between each batch instance when batch_size > 1

templateId.description: Optional reference to a track template if this track is an instance of a template

templateParameters.description: Parameters to customize this track instance if it's based on a template

priority.description: Track priority for auto-planning (lower number = higher priority, default: 100)

steps.$comment: Sequential steps are time:ProperInterval instances. Within a track, consecutive steps relate by time:intervalMeets (no gap) or time:intervalBefore (with gap). The track time:intervalContains each step

priority.description: Priority for resource allocation (lower number = higher priority, default: 100)

flex.$comment: Adjustable time:Duration — the step's extent can expand within [minDuration, maxDuration] bounds to satisfy temporal constraints
flex.description: Flexible timing settings for the step

enabled.description: Whether this step can be flexibly timed

mode.description: Flex mode: 'fill' expands to fill gap to next step, 'max' extends to maximum duration

minDuration.description: Minimum duration for flexible steps. Can be a number (seconds) or a string with time units

maxDuration.description: Maximum duration for flexible steps. Can be a number (seconds) or a string with time units

task.description: Reference to a resource constraint this step requires

tasks.description: References to resource constraints this step requires

taskResources.description: References to resource constraints with fractional usage

fraction.description: Fraction of the resource used (0.0 to 1.0)

codeBlock.description: Code to execute when the step starts

description.description: Description of what the code does

startTrigger.$comment: Defines a time:hasBeginning constraint — the step's start time:Instant is determined by a temporal relation to another interval or an external event

oneOf.$comment: Compound temporal constraint — 'all' requires conjunction of Allen relations (all must hold simultaneously); 'any' requires disjunction (earliest satisfied relation determines the time:hasBeginning)
oneOf.description: Multiple start triggers with logical operators

logic.description: Logic for multiple triggers: 'all' means ALL triggers must be satisfied, 'any' means ANY ONE trigger can start the step

duration.$comment: time:hasTemporalDuration — the step's duration is a time:Duration (fixed), a bounded time:Duration (variable), or an open-ended time:ProperInterval (indefinite)
duration.description: Defines the duration behavior of the step

type.$comment: time:Duration with time:numericDuration and time:unitType time:unitSecond

seconds.$comment: time:numericDuration — exact extent of the time:Duration
seconds.description: Duration. Can be a number (seconds) or a string with time units (e.g., '30s', '5m', '1h')

type.$comment: Bounded time:Duration — the actual extent is constrained between minSeconds and maxSeconds
type.description: Step has a variable duration that can be ended manually

minSeconds.description: Minimum duration. Can be a number (seconds) or a string with time units (e.g., '2m', '1h')

maxSeconds.description: Maximum duration. Can be a number (seconds) or a string with time units (e.g., '5m', '2h')

defaultSeconds.description: Default duration if not manually ended. Can be a number (seconds) or a string with time units (e.g., '3m', '1h30m')

optimalSeconds.description: Optimal duration used by the planner for optimization. Can be a number (seconds) or a string with time units (e.g., '2m30s', '1h')

triggerName.description: Optional name for the manual end trigger

type.$comment: time:ProperInterval with time:hasBeginning (known time:Instant) but no determined time:hasEnd — end is an externally triggered time:Instant

defaultSeconds.description: Expected duration for timeline display. Can be a number (seconds) or a string with time units (e.g., '5m', '1h')

triggerName.description: Optional name for the manual end trigger

preBuffer.$comment: A time:ProperInterval that time:intervalMeets the step — the preBuffer's time:hasEnd equals the step's time:hasBeginning
preBuffer.description: Optional buffer time before the step starts (setup/preparation time)

duration.description: Buffer duration. Can be a number (seconds) or a string with time units (e.g., '30s', '2m')

description.description: Description of what happens during the pre-buffer (e.g., 'Equipment setup', 'Room preparation')

tasks.description: Resources required during the pre-buffer period

taskResources.description: Resources with fractional usage during the pre-buffer period

fraction.description: Fraction of the resource used (0.0 to 1.0)

postBuffer.$comment: A time:ProperInterval that time:intervalMetBy the step — the postBuffer's time:hasBeginning equals the step's time:hasEnd
postBuffer.description: Optional buffer time after the step completes (cleanup/teardown time)

duration.description: Buffer duration. Can be a number (seconds) or a string with time units (e.g., '30s', '2m')

description.description: Description of what happens during the post-buffer (e.g., 'Equipment cleanup', 'Data backup')

tasks.description: Resources required during the post-buffer period

taskResources.description: Resources with fractional usage during the post-buffer period

fraction.description: Fraction of the resource used (0.0 to 1.0)

metadata.description: Additional custom metadata for the step. Recognized convention for the fold view (see rhylthyme.fold_view.program_to_fold): 'fold' set to "prep" forces this step to render as a banner prep-note instead of a merge-tree row/op; 'foldLabel' overrides the auto-derived column label for this step's fold-view operation.

choice.description: Defines a choice point where the user selects one of several paths. Downstream steps with a matching choiceId on their afterStep trigger only execute if that choice is selected. The first option is the default if the user does not choose.

prompt.description: Question or prompt to display to the user (e.g., 'Which protein would you like?')

options.description: Available choices — the first option is the default

choiceId.description: Unique identifier for this choice option

canAbort.description: Whether this step can be aborted (default: false)

resourceConstraints.description: Defines resource constraints for task types

maxConcurrent.description: Maximum number of concurrent steps allowed for this task type

trackTemplates.description: Reusable track templates that can be instantiated multiple times

templateId.description: Unique identifier for the track template

name.description: Human-readable name for the track template

description.description: Detailed description of the track template

parameterSchema.description: JSON Schema defining the parameters this template accepts

steps.description: Step definitions for this template, similar to track steps but may include parameter references

metadata.description: Additional custom metadata for the program

thumbnail.description: URL of the program's hero image. May be an absolute URL (e.g. Supabase Storage public URL or external source like TheMealDB) or a relative reference.

replicates.$comment: Generates multiple time:ProperInterval instances. mode=parallel: all share the same time:hasBeginning (time:intervalStarts). mode=stagger: successive beginnings offset by a time:Duration (time:intervalAfter). mode=serial: each time:intervalMetBy its predecessor
replicates.description: Replicate this track or step multiple times with configurable execution mode

mode.description: Execution mode: 'parallel' runs all at once, 'stagger' adds delay between starts, 'serial' chains sequentially

delay.description: Delay between starts for stagger mode. Can be a number (seconds) or a string with time units (e.g., '1m30s', '1h')

singleStartTrigger.$comment: Encodes a temporal relation (Allen's interval algebra) between this step's time:ProperInterval and a reference interval or time:Instant

type.$comment: time:intervalMetBy (event=end, no offset) — this step's time:hasBeginning equals the referenced step's time:hasEnd. With offsetSeconds > 0: time:intervalAfter. With event=start: this step's beginning aligns with the referenced step's beginning (time:intervalStarts or time:intervalOverlaps)
type.description: Step starts immediately after another step ends

stepId.description: ID of the step that must complete before this one starts

event.$comment: Selects which time:Instant of the referenced time:ProperInterval anchors the relation: time:hasEnd (default) or time:hasBeginning
event.description: Whether to trigger after the referenced step's start or end (default: end)

offsetSeconds.description: Offset in seconds from the referenced step's end (or start if event='start'). Can be negative to start before the referenced step ends — negative offsets require the referenced step to have duration.type='indefinite'. Can be a number or a string with time units (e.g., '5m', '-20m')

choiceId.description: If the referenced step has a 'choice' property, this step only executes when the user selects the matching choiceId. Steps without choiceId always execute regardless of the choice.

type.$comment: time:intervalAfter — a gap (time:Duration of bufferSeconds) separates the referenced step's time:hasEnd from this step's time:hasBeginning
type.description: Step starts after another step ends plus a buffer time

stepId.description: ID of the step that must complete before this one starts

event.description: Whether to trigger after the referenced step's start or end (default: end)

bufferSeconds.description: Buffer time after the referenced step. Can be a number (seconds) or a string with time units (e.g., '30s', '2m')

type.$comment: This step's time:hasBeginning equals the program's time:hasBeginning (same time:Instant)
type.description: Step starts when the program starts

type.$comment: time:intervalAfter the program's time:hasBeginning — a time:Duration of offsetSeconds separates the program start time:Instant from this step's time:hasBeginning
type.description: Step starts after an offset from program start

offsetSeconds.description: Offset from program start. Can be a number (seconds) or a string with time units (e.g., '5m', '1h30m')

type.$comment: This step's time:hasBeginning is an externally determined time:Instant — not derivable from any temporal relation to other intervals

triggerName.description: Optional name for the manual trigger

type.$comment: This step's time:hasBeginning coincides with an interruption time:Instant of the referenced step — not a standard Allen relation; models exceptional/contingent temporal ordering
type.description: Step starts when another step is aborted

stepId.description: ID of the step that must be aborted for this one to start
